unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts two things. First, the mind's refusal to imagine itself at rest or in a straight line, which is why Adams 'was forced, as usual, to let it imagine something else'. The redefinition now follows the dictionary with no stated reason. Second, it cuts the habit-versus-novelty classes that give 'unequally inert' its content.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The core definition and 'movement of inertia' around habitual motives remain.

evidence.quote: Finding that his mind refused to imagine itself at rest or in a straight line, he was forced, as usual, to let it imagine something else
His mind refused to imagine itself at rest or in a straight line, so he was forced, as usual, to let it imagine something else.
Since the question concerned the mind, and not matter, he decided from personal experience that his mind was never at rest
One class of minds responded only to habit; another only to novelty.
had gone on complaining that minds were unequally inert. No two men thought alike, and no woman thought like a man.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'His mind refused ... imagine something else' sentence, and reinsert 'One class of minds responded only to habit; another only to novelty.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan lists the redefinition and 'Minds are unequally inert' as essential.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The professed-ignorance method that turns physics into psychology disappears, and 'unequally inert' becomes an empty assertion just before race and sex are introduced.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Inertia redefinition loses its comic motivation and its defining contrast

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Three things the first draft kept are cut: the qualified doubt that race-inertia was ever overcome without destroying the race; the sentence that the American woman's movement mattered 'infinitely' more than any race; and the claim that this was 'the most vital of all problems of force' to be solved in one generation. Paragraph 13 now ends on Americans ignoring sex.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Paragraph 19 still names 'inertia of race and inertia of sex' as vital to America.

evidence.quote: History looked doubtful when asked whether race-inertia had ever been overcome without destroying the race in order to reconstruct it
Yet the task of accelerating or deflecting the movement of the American woman had interest infinitely greater than that of any race whatever, Russian or Chinese, Asiatic or African.
This problem needed to be solved in one generation of American women, and was the most vital of all problems of force.
The American always ostentatiously ignored sex, and American history mentioned hardly the name of a woman.
Inertia of race and bulk might in time perhaps be partially overcome.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's closing sentence of paragraph 13 ('Yet the task ...'). Optionally restore the 'History looked doubtful' clause.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: 'Race-inertia is constant ... Americans ignore sex' and the Russia/America ending are essential.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Without these sentences the argument never explains why the American woman displaces Russia as the central problem. The final comparison, Russia 'somewhat easier' than America and race inertia possibly overcome while sex inertia cannot be without extinction, loses its prepared contrast.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Race-to-sex pivot and American urgency removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'for himself, the game--not the stakes--was the chief interest' and 'The figures, not the facts, concerned his chart'. It also drops every listed position on the chart, so 'These were the positions' refers back to a single sentence about China.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The insect, 'seemed to him fixed', and 'the game seemed lost' still frame the outlook as Adams's forecast.

evidence.quote: for himself, the game--not the stakes--was the chief interest
Japan must make the best terms she could; England must go on receding; America and Germany would look on at the avalanche.
To the humble student, the loss of Hay's game affected only Hay; for himself, the game--not the stakes--was the chief interest.
These were the positions charted on the map of political unity by an insect in Washington in the spring of 1903, and they seemed to him fixed.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'To the humble student ...' sentence, and either 'Russia held Europe and America in her grasp, and Cassini held Hay in his' or the Japan/England line.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan lists the insect's chart and the lost game as essential.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The self-mocking insect who coolly charts Hay's defeat as an equation loses its ironic distance, and the forecast loses its concrete shape.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Student's detachment and the insect's chart thinned

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts the Washington-society coda ending 'and the tenth bored her' and the opening 'Gay or serious' frame. The paragraph now stops on the plain 'at forty her task was over.'
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The family, Church/State and age-forty points all survive.

evidence.quote: had created only a medley where nine men out of ten refused her request to be civilized, and the tenth bored her
where nine men out of ten refused her request to be civilized, and the tenth bored her.
Never had the world known a more capable or devoted mother, but at forty her task was over.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's final sentence ('She was left with no stage ... the tenth bored her').
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required section; its execution matters to the voice profile.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The signature periodic build ending in an epigram is lost, and the bitterness reads as summary rather than Adams's irony.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Clever-woman paragraph loses its deflating close

unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'No refuge except such as the man created' still partly motivates the 'must'.

she was sexless; she had discarded all that the male disliked. She must, like the man, marry machinery.
